text:
Maya: Morning — overnight evals threw a notable spike on the Legal-Snippets promptset for the quant4-int8 bringup. ~14% fail rate vs baseline. Failures are mostly truncated or returned boilerplate/policy text instead of completing the clause. Samples below.

Maya: ```
input: "Please complete the following contract clause: The Lessee shall..."
quant4-int8 output: "*** This content is restricted. Contact support.***"
fp16 output: "The Lessee shall maintain insurance..."
```

Alex: Ack. Is this isolated to quant4-int8 or seen on other compression configs too? Any diffs in tokenization? :eyes:

Maya: Quick check: fp16 baseline looks fine, int8-fp4 also mostly fine. Spike localizes to quant4-int8 kernel combo on a subset of sequences with long parentheses/URLs.

Sam: Possible tokenization edge — long parentheses + legal citations tend to create weird token boundaries after kvcache snapshotting. I can run a small reproduce harness against the failing promptset.

Jordan: Assigning owners: Alex for infra/serving config, Sam for tokenizer/repro, Maya keeps eval owner. Severity suggested P2 (degraded quality across a cohort). Thoughts?

Alex: I can check recent kernel swap and fallback policy logs. Will grep deploy logs for recent patches on that node pool (likely rolled last night).

DeployBot: Incident created INC-2026-984, alert threshold exceeded for suite "Legal-Snippets". Tags: quant4, int8, eval. Assigned to eng-ml oncall channel.

Sam: Repro plan: (1) run failing prompts on quant4-int8 with kv-cache warm vs cold, (2) compare tokenizer outputs for the truncated samples, (3) run with a debug build to capture attention weights if needed. I'll post a small script in the thread in ~30m.

Maya: Attaching cohort IDs and sample indices in the eval dashboard: cohort_id=lg-2026-03, sample_indices=[12,47,128,204]. If anyone needs direct links ping me.

Alex: Found recent kernel selection tweak on the runtime (slotting zlib-opt into int8 path) at 02:12 UTC. Rolling that change back on a small canary should be quick — will coordinate with Sam's repro to avoid flapping.

Jordan: Good. Next steps: Sam to repro and confirm root cause, Alex to rollback canary if repro matches, Maya to update eval alert status and communicate to CS if customer-facing models affected. I'll set a 2-hour check-in. :white_check_mark:

Maya: Thanks — starting repro run now and will post logs.

Sam: Posting initial repro summary in 20m.

Alex: If rollback needed, I'll target 03:15 UTC canary window.

Maya: Marking alert as "investigating" in dashboard.

Jordan: Thanks team. We'll reconvene at the check-in or sooner if blocking.
